issues.legal_issue: A trespass does not end merely because the trespassers express regret or seek permission to continue, and the person whose property is being trespassed upon may prevent its continuation.
material_facts: The carts remained inside the field when the protest and violence occurred; they had not reached the public passage.
The carts were still several yards inside the field, and the trespass therefore remained in progress.
The trespassers had to cross further parts of the field to reach the public passage.
issues.conclusion: The trespass was still in progress, so the property holder could prevent its continuation. The trespassers had to abide by the property holder’s directions and had no right to insist on proceeding further through the field.
issues.legal_principle: The right of private defence of property includes the right to prevent an ongoing criminal trespass. The trespass does not end merely because the trespassers regret their conduct or seek to continue far enough to leave the property. The judgment identifies no specific numbered provision or earlier case as the basis for this principle.

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal challenging criminal convictions.
predicates.trespass_still_in_progress: The trespassers and their property remained on the land and had not completed the trespass.
predicates.property_holder_objected: The person whose land was being trespassed upon objected to the trespass.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal concerns a trespass that is still in progress and the property holder objects, the property holder may prevent the trespass from continuing.

issues.legal_issue: Members of an unlawful assembly may be liable for murder when they pursue a common object by force, are prepared to use weapons if thwarted, and know that death is a likely consequence of that violence.
material_facts: The group took a longer route through several fields despite a shorter available route, causing damage to crops and making objections foreseeable.
The group’s common object was to take the carts through the fields to reach the public passage and to use force if obstructed.
Several members carried lathis and one carried a hatchet; the court concluded that the group was prepared to use those weapons if thwarted.
The victim suffered multiple injuries, including serious head wounds, and died from the injuries inflicted by the group’s concerted acts.
issues.conclusion: The group was prepared to use violence in prosecution of its common object and knew that death was a likely result of that violence. The victim’s death was caused in prosecution of the common object, making the offence murder, for which the members were liable under section 302 read with section 149 of the Indian Penal Code.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 149 of the Indian Penal Code, members of an unlawful assembly may be held liable for an offence committed in prosecution of its common object. The court concluded from the group’s weapons, readiness to use them if obstructed, and the circumstances of the chosen route that the members knew death was a likely consequence; it upheld liability for murder under section 302 read with section 149. The judgment cites no earlier cases for this conclusion.
